title: An animation studio that renders at night
summary: A Guadalajara studio renders a short film overnight on 200 VMs that read the same scenes. The artists work from their office and no scene can be lost.

requirements.1: {{s1}} holds the project folder that hundreds of Linux servers mount at the same time over NFS, available in both zones.
requirements.2: {{s2}} keeps last night's version of the project folder, so a scene someone deletes by mistake can be recovered.
requirements.3: {{s3}} stores the finished frames for years; they are read over HTTP and survive the loss of an entire zone.
requirements.4: {{s4}} provides the render nodes: they can shut down with seconds or minutes of notice because the job resumes, and the lowest price with no commitment matters.
requirements.5: {{s5}} joins the office to the cloud network today, encrypted, over the internet it already has.
requirements.6: The artists work at the studio office in Guadalajara and upload their scenes from there.

s1.explanation: A regional Filestore instance fails over transparently if a zone fails, and many application instances use the same file system at the same time over NFS. Filestore is available in northamerica-south1, with three zones.
s1.hint_cue: mount at the same time over NFS

s2.explanation: A Filestore backup is a point-in-time copy with all the instance data, meant for disaster recovery. A replica, by contrast, is updated continuously with every change on the source.

s3.explanation: A regional Cloud Storage bucket stores data in at least two zones and is designed to tolerate the loss of any one of them. A zonal Filestore instance becomes unavailable if its zone goes down.
s3.hint_cue: survive the loss of an entire zone

s4.explanation: Spot VMs get a preemption notice (Google recommends 120 seconds), have no minimum or maximum runtime, and have discounts of up to 91% off the on-demand price.

s5.explanation: Cloud VPN extends the office network to the VPC through an IPsec VPN connection that encrypts traffic between the two networks, and HA VPN provides a 99.99% or 99.9% SLA depending on the topology.
s5.hint_cue: over the internet it already has

gcp-persistent-disk.s1: Persistent Disk is only shared between VMs in the same zone, with at most 2 VMs in multi-writer mode, and almost no file system is built for shared block storage.
gcp-persistent-disk.s3: Persistent Disk is block storage for VMs; it does not serve the frames over HTTP.

gcp-filestore-replication.s2: The replica is a complete copy updated continuously with every change on the source and cannot be mounted, so it does not keep last night's version.
gcp-filestore-replication.s1: Instance replication copies an existing instance to another region; on its own it is not the folder the servers mount.

gcp-filestore-zonal.s3: A zonal Filestore instance becomes unavailable if its zone fails, until that zone is restored, and it is read over NFS, not HTTP.
gcp-filestore-zonal.s1: A zonal instance lives in a single zone and becomes unavailable if that zone fails; the requirement asks for both zones.

gcp-cud.s4: A committed use discount lowers the price in exchange for committing to usage or spend for one or three years, and the requirement asks for no commitment.

gcp-interconnect.s5: Cloud Interconnect is a separate link that does not cross the public internet, and with Partner Interconnect you must add IPsec encryption separately.
